chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: location fits event-to-place relation; SportsEvent and MusicEvent are both events, and the object is a MusicEvent (a type of event) that serves as the location.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: foodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A food establishment relation between a cook action and the specific place or food establishment where the cooking occurred. Also called: cooking location, restaurant, kitchen. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food establishment "Gourmet Restaurant", "Home Cook makes dinner" food establishment "My Kitchen", "Baker bakes bread" food establishment "Local Bakery". Distinct from foodEvent, which is a specific event.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

chosen_property.label: participant
chosen_property.justification: participant covers all event-to-entity relations; objects are countries, groups, recordings, persons, compositions, all valid participants.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: numberOfPlayers
candidates.comment: The number of people who can play a game or video game series, often expressed as a minimum, maximum, or range. Also called player count, game capacity, participant number. Examples: "Board Game X numberOfPlayers '2-4'", "Video Game Y numberOfPlayers '1 (single-player)'", "Online Game Z numberOfPlayers '100 (max)'".

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: location directly matches event-to-place; City and StadiumOrArena are places.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: homeLocation
candidates.comment: A home location relation between a person and their residential contact point or place. Also called residence, dwelling, home address. Examples: "A person has a home location in London.", "Her home location is a specific address.", "The individual's home location is a contact point."

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: workLocation
candidates.comment: A work location relation between a person and a contact point or place, identifying where the person performs their professional duties. Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. Distinct from homeLocation, which is a person's residential address.

candidates.label: globalLocationNumber
candidates.comment: A global location number relation between an organization, person, or place and its unique 13-digit GLN identifier. Also called: GLN, International Location Number, ILN. Examples: "Acme Corp Warehouse" global location number "1234567890123", "Hospital Main Campus" global location number "9876543210987", "Distribution Center X" global location number "1122334455667".

chosen_property.label: date
chosen_property.definition: The date on which an event occurs.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses event date; minted 'date' as a general event date property.

candidates.label: dateRead
candidates.comment: A temporal interaction relation between a message and the date/time it was read by the recipient. Also called: read date, message read time, recipient read time. Examples: "Email" date read "2023-10-26T10:30:00Z", "Chat Message" date read "2023-10-26T10:35:00Z". Distinct from dateReceived, which is when the message arrived.

candidates.label: dateSent
candidates.comment: A temporal dispatch relation between a message and the date/time it was sent. Also called: sending date, message dispatch time, transmission time. Examples: "Email" date sent "2023-10-26T10:20:00Z", "SMS Message" date sent "2023-10-26T10:30:00Z". Distinct from dateReceived, which is when the message arrived.

candidates.label: dateCreated
candidates.comment: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: birthDate
candidates.comment: A date representing a person's birth. Also called: date of birth, birthday. Examples: "Person 'John Doe' birthDate '1980-05-15'", "Person 'Jane Smith' birthDate '1992-11-22'."

candidates.label: datePosted
candidates.comment: A temporal publication relation between a CDCPMD record, job posting, real estate listing, or special announcement and its online publication date. Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.

candidates.label: dateIssued
candidates.comment: A temporal issuance relation between a ticket and the date it was issued. Also called: issuance date, date of issue, ticket date. Examples: "Concert Ticket" date issued "2023-04-01", "Flight Ticket" date issued "2023-01-10T14:30:00Z", "Parking Permit" date issued "2023-07-01".

candidates.label: dateVehicleFirstRegistered
candidates.comment: A temporal registration relation between a vehicle and the date of its first registration with public authorities. Also called: first registration date, initial registration, vehicle registration date. Examples: "Car" date vehicle first registered "2018-03-15", "Motorcycle" date vehicle first registered "2020-07-01", "Truck" date vehicle first registered "2015-11-20".

candidates.label: dateModified
candidates.comment: A temporal revision relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was most recently modified. Also called: last modified date, revision date, update date. Examples: "Wikipedia Article" date modified "2023-10-26T11:45:00Z", "Software Documentation" date modified "2023-09-01", "Data Feed Entry" date modified "2023-01-05". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the initial creation date.

chosen_property.label: result
chosen_property.justification: result fits action-to-outcome; SportsEvent is an action-like event and the object is another SportsEvent as outcome.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: afterMedia
candidates.comment: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: yield
candidates.comment: A yield relation between a how-to guide and a quantitative value or text, specifying the quantity or type of output produced by following the instructions. Also called output quantity, resulting amount, production yield. Examples: HowToRecipe yield "12 cookies", HowToCraft yield "1 paper airplane", HowToGuide yield "5 liters of jam".

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

chosen_property.label: score
chosen_property.definition: The score or points achieved by a participant in a competitive event.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly links an event to a country's score; minted 'score' for event-to-country score relation.

candidates.label: ratingValue
candidates.comment: A rating value relation between a rating and its numerical or textual score. Also called score, rating score, value of rating. Examples: "A movie review has a rating value of 4.5.", "A product has a rating value of 'Excellent'.", "A restaurant has a rating value of 3 stars."

candidates.label: bestRating
candidates.comment: A number or text representing the highest value allowed in a rating system. Also called: maximum rating, top score, highest possible rating. Examples: "Rating 'Product Review' bestRating '5'", "Rating 'Movie Score' bestRating '10'". Distinct from worstRating, which is the lowest value.

candidates.label: algorithm
candidates.comment: An algorithm relation between a medical risk score and the set of rules or computational method used to calculate it. Also called calculation method, scoring rules, computation logic. Examples: "A medical risk score's algorithm is 'Framingham Risk Score formula'.", "The diagnostic score's algorithm is 'CHA2DS2-VASc'."

candidates.label: aggregateRating
candidates.comment: An aggregate rating relation between an item (e.g., product, service, creative work) and its overall rating derived from multiple reviews. Also called overall score, collective rating, average review. Examples: "A product's aggregate rating is '4.5 stars'.", "A movie's aggregate rating is '8.2/10'."

candidates.label: reviewRating
candidates.comment: The specific rating provided within a review. Also called rating in review, review's score, individual rating. Examples: `Customer Review` reviewRating `5 stars`, `Film Critic Review` reviewRating `8/10`, `Restaurant Review` reviewRating `3 out of 5`. Distinct from `aggregateRating`, which is the overall rating of the review *as a creative work*, not the rating *given by* the review.

candidates.label: worstRating
candidates.comment: A worst rating relation between a rating and a number or text, specifying the lowest possible value within that rating system. Also called minimum rating, lowest score, bottom value. Examples: RatingSystem worstRating 1, ReviewRating worstRating "Terrible", StarRating worstRating 0. Distinct from bestRating, which specifies the highest possible value.

candidates.label: ratingCount
candidates.comment: A rating count relation between an aggregate rating and the total number of individual ratings contributing to it. Also called number of ratings, total ratings. Examples: "An aggregate rating has a rating count of 150.", "A product review summary has a rating count of 500.", "A movie's average rating has a rating count of 10,000."

candidates.label: musicBy
candidates.comment: A composer or music group responsible for the soundtrack of a creative work. Also called soundtrack by, composer of, musical score by. Examples: "Movie X musicBy 'John Williams'", "TV Series Y musicBy 'Ramin Djawadi'", "Video Game Z musicBy 'Koji Kondo'". Distinct from composer, which is for the composer of a MusicComposition.

candidates.label: reviewCount
candidates.comment: The total number of individual reviews contributing to an aggregate rating. Also called total reviews, number of reviews, review tally. Examples: `Product Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `150`, `Movie Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `5000`, `Service Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `75`.

candidates.label: starRating
candidates.comment: An official quality rating for a food establishment or lodging business, typically from a standards body. Also called "official rating", "quality rating", "hotel stars", "restaurant rating". Examples: "The hotel has starRating 5 stars", "The restaurant's starRating is 3 Michelin stars", "This lodging business received a 4-star rating.". Distinct from aggregateRating, which is a summary of user-generated reviews.

chosen_property.label: target
chosen_property.justification: target fits action-to-object; BoycottEvent is an action and Country is the target.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: targetName
candidates.comment: A textual name of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node name", "educational standard name", "learning objective name". Examples: "The alignment object has targetName 'Algebra I'", "The educational framework node's targetName is 'Critical Thinking'", "This targetName identifies a specific skill."

candidates.label: targetUrl
candidates.comment: A URL identifying a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node URL", "educational standard URL", "learning objective URL". Examples: "The alignment object has targetUrl 'http://example.com/algebra-standard'", "The educational framework node's targetUrl points to its definition", "This targetUrl links to a specific competency."

candidates.label: targetProduct
candidates.comment: A compatibility relation between software source code and the software application or operating system it is intended for. Also called "compatible with", "designed for", "applies to product", "software target". Examples: "The source code has targetProduct Windows 10", "The script's targetProduct is Microsoft Excel", "This code is written for targetProduct Linux."

candidates.label: targetPlatform
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of platform for which an API reference is intended, such as phone or desktop. Also called "platform type", "development platform", "operating system target", "device target". Examples: "The API reference has targetPlatform iOS", "The software's targetPlatform is Windows Desktop", "This API is designed for targetPlatform Android."

candidates.label: targetDescription
candidates.comment: A textual description of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node description", "educational standard description", "learning objective description". Examples: "The alignment object has targetDescription 'Understand basic algebra'", "The educational framework node's targetDescription explains the competency", "This targetDescription details a specific learning outcome."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: targetCollection
candidates.comment: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.

candidates.label: targetPopulation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the characteristics of the intended or typical population for a dietary supplement or dose schedule. Also called "intended users", "demographic target", "user group", "audience characteristics". Examples: "The supplement has targetPopulation 'adults'", "The dose schedule's targetPopulation is 'children aged 6-12'", "This product is designed for a targetPopulation of athletes."

candidates.label: audience
candidates.comment: An intended group for whom a creative work, event, lodging business, play action, product, or service was created. Also called: target group, demographic, intended recipient. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Children's Book' audience 'Children'", "Event 'Tech Conference' audience 'Developers'", "Product 'Luxury Car' audience 'High-net-worth individuals'."

chosen_property.label: reason
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the cause or explanation for a situation, often referencing a show.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses reason for an event; minted 'reason' as a general cause relation.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: ratingExplanation
candidates.comment: A rating explanation relation between a rating and a brief text providing context or justification for the rating. Also called rating justification, explanation for rating, rating context. Examples: "A product rating includes a rating explanation 'The battery life was excellent, but the camera was disappointing'.", "A fact-check rating has a rating explanation 'The claim was partially true, lacking full context'.", "A service rating has a rating explanation 'The staff were friendly, but wait times were long'."

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: answerExplanation
candidates.comment: An answer explanation relation between an answer and a comment or web content providing a detailed clarification or step-by-step reasoning. Also called solution explanation, answer justification, detailed response. Examples: "An answer's answer explanation details the calculation steps.", "The correct answer's explanation clarifies the underlying principle."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: healthCondition

candidates.label: about

Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: discusses
candidates.comment: A discussion relation between a user comment and the creative work it is associated with. Also called "comments on", "pertains to", "about". Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.

candidates.label: manufacturer

candidates.label: duration

Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: gender
candidates.comment: A gender relation between a person or sports team and their gender identity or classification. Also called: sex, gender identity, team gender. Examples: "John Doe" gender "Male", "Jane Smith" gender "Female", "Mixed Doubles Team" gender "Mixed".

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: author
candidates.comment: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

chosen_property.label: source
chosen_property.justification: source fits statement-to-origin; objects are the sources of the statements.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: costOrigin
candidates.comment: A source relation between a drug cost and additional details about where the cost data originated. Also called: cost data source, price origin, expense source. Examples: "Drug X cost" cost origin "Medicare Part B", "Medication Y price" cost origin "Private Insurance", "Prescription Z expense" cost origin "Manufacturer's List Price".

candidates.label: evidenceOrigin

Distinct from evidenceLevel, which is the strength of the evidence.

candidates.label: isBasedOnUrl
candidates.comment: A source URL relation between a creative work and a specific URL that served as a resource for its creation. Also called source URL, derived from URL, based on URL, reference URL. Examples: A research paper has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://arxiv.org/abs/1234.5678'. A blog post has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://example.com/original-article'. A web page has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://old-version.com/page'. Distinct from isBasedOn, which can refer to any CreativeWork or Product, not just a URL.

candidates.label: sourceOrganization
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a creative work and the organization on whose behalf its creator was working. Also called "commissioning organization", "producing organization", "organization behind", "publisher organization". Examples: "The research paper's sourceOrganization was MIT", "The documentary's sourceOrganization was BBC", "This report's sourceOrganization is the World Health Organization."

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

candidates.label: codeRepository
candidates.comment: A location relation for software source code, providing a URL to its repository. Also called "source code URL", "repository link", "code host". Examples: "Software project codeRepository 'https://github.com/example/project'", "Library source code codeRepository 'https://svn.example.org/repo'".

candidates.label: citation
candidates.comment: A reference relation between a creative work and another creative work or text that it cites. Also called "reference", "cited work", "source". Examples: "Research paper citation 'Smith, J. (2020). Article Title.'", "Blog post citation 'https://example.com/article'".

candidates.label: originalMediaLink
candidates.comment: A link to the original version of media content, such as a web page or a direct media object file, in a media review. Also called source media link, original content URL, primary media source. Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaLink 'https://originalsource.com/video123'", "Image Review B originalMediaLink 'https://archive.org/image456'", "Audio Review C originalMediaLink 'https://podcast.example.com/episode789'". candidates.label: performTime

candidates.label: performerIn
